sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Eindhoven is moving to paid parking everywhere inside its Ring and to a Ring that through traffic cannot cross. Paid parking applies in the whole area inside the Ring and in some other places, from 09:00 to 21:00 every day including Sundays and holidays [2]. The council adopted the parking tax ordinance on 4 November 2025, applying from 1 January 2026: 4.50 euros an hour plus a 0.30 start charge in the centre, 2.55 euros in the inner-ring Schilwijk areas, 2.10 euros outside the Ring and 4.50 euros in Strijp-S [3]. A first resident permit in the centre costs 11.79 euros a month and a second 24.71, with a maximum of two permits per address [4]. A gazette of 12 May 2026 publishes the city's parking standards for new development, stating the aim that the whole area inside the Ring becomes fully paid parking and a policy aim of no new car parking spaces in the city centre; this governs development plans, not existing parking [1]. A decision published on 29 July 2026 adds permit-based parking in three more areas [5].

The traffic circulation plan is planned to divide the area inside the Ring into four sectors with traffic filters open only to pedestrians, cyclists, buses and emergency services, while destinations inside the Ring, including car parks, stay reachable by car [7]. A zero-emission zone for vans and trucks has applied since 1 January 2025, and a milieuzone for diesel cars of class 4 and lower is to start on 1 January 2027 [8]; the court found the justification for the zone at De Kade insufficient on 27 May 2025 [9]. The new coalition keeps paid parking inside the ring road and plans four park-and-ride or traffic hub sites at the city edge, according to Omroep Brabant [10]. Enforcement is by scan car, with the assessment posted to the owner [6].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Eindhoven has two park-and-ride sites. Genneper Parken, opened in 2021 at a cost of over 20 million euros, has 641 spaces and is open 24/7 [11]; in December 2021 Omroep Brabant reported that it was used by on average 25 people a day, about 4 percent occupancy, costing the city about 300,000 euros a year, an old report that is not current usage [12]. P+R Meerhoven has 231 spaces at 1.50 euros for the first hour and a daily maximum of 4 euros [13]. For electric vehicles, the city installs public charge points through a concession with Vattenfall InCharge over the coming two to four years [17], and Q-Park lists 20 charge points at Stadhuisplein [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Q-Park lists city-centre and edge garages with capacities of 1,150 spaces at Mathildelaan, 1,143 at Heuvel, 796 at Kennedyplein, 510 at De Bijenkorf, 347 at Centrum De Admirant, 306 at Stadhuisplein, 246 at Witte Dame and 150 at Hooghuis, and says it works together with the municipality [14].

Our data cover two of these: Witte Dame (242 spaces in the feed) and the Fuutlaan park-and-ride (150), 392 spaces measured for 61 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 37% on weekdays and 36% at weekends, weighted by spaces. Fuutlaan averaged 50% on weekdays and 53% at weekends and reached full in a single Saturday-noon reading. Witte Dame averaged 29% on weekdays and 24% at weekends and reached full once, on a Sunday at 13:00. These are two of the ten garages and say little about the whole centre. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
